title: Use the supported test API, and state what a test proves
observed: The behavioral-testing material uses AgentTest, say() and list-style session.run examples. Those interfaces do not match the installed Agents 1.8.11 test surface inspected for this project.
correction: Use AgentSession.run(user_input=...), its RunResult and the supported event assertions or mock_tools. A passing model-behavior test is evidence about the exercised conversation, not proof of real audio delivery, durable acceptance or exactly one external effect.
book_action: Add a worked behavior-test question beside the existing deterministic and actual-media evidence requirements.

title: Filter before releasing the original stream
observed: The content-filtering example buffers text for sentence checks while also yielding original chunks when no sentence boundary is present. Even after repairing surrounding API compatibility, this logic can release a disallowed prefix to downstream speech before the later check. This is a static finding; no live leak was exercised.
correction: Define the release unit, hold it until the required check succeeds, bound the pending buffer, and specify rejection and timeout behavior. The example's moderator parsing failure also returns safe=True, which contradicts its stated conservative fallback.
book_action: Add an output-admission timeline and follow-ups about latency, partial release and fail-open policy.

title: Bind retrieval to the actual hook and caller turn
observed: The RAG material includes a one-argument on_user_turn_completed implementation and context helpers that do not match the inspected SDK contract. Its caching examples also use normalized-query hashes while discussing semantic matching.
correction: The pinned hook receives turn_ctx and new_message. Use the supported context API; bound retrieval and preserve turn identity, current access, source freshness and document scope. An exact normalized-query cache and an embedding-similarity cache require different lookup and validation logic.
book_action: Add two questions covering interrupted retrieval and scope-aware evidence caching. Keep retrieved instructions as untrusted data.

title: Separate SIP room placement from agent dispatch
observed: Several phone lessons imply that a room-name prefix selects the intended registered agent. A prefix can determine room naming without establishing named-agent selection.
correction: Trace both decisions: the SIP dispatch rule places the SIP participant in a room; agent dispatch selects and starts the intended agent job. Configure the agent explicitly where appropriate, for example through the room configuration's agent list, and observe job readiness separately from caller placement.
book_action: Add a SIP-to-room-to-agent diagram and the failure case where the call joins but the intended agent never starts.

title: A server-side signing secret does not authorize token requests
observed: The educational frontend token examples omit an application-user authentication and authorization boundary while accepting room or identity inputs. This is an omission in the shown example, not a tested vulnerability in the Academy website.
correction: Authenticate the application user and derive or authorize the room, participant identity, dispatch and grants on the server. Metadata and caller-provided labels do not establish tenant access or business consent.
book_action: Add a token-minting review question with wrong-room and overbroad-grant follow-ups.

title: Use each realtime data API for its own contract
observed: The frontend RPC example uses an AgentSession rpc_request event instead of the inspected room/local-participant RPC method registration. Other examples imply that reliable data delivery provides arbitrary-file transport or proves a device performed an action.
correction: Use supported RPC registration for request/response, attributes for suitable synchronized state, and streams for larger payloads. Transport reliability is separate from durable business acceptance and from physical execution. Reconcile an ambiguous command by its original identity.
book_action: Add an RPC-versus-stream-versus-state decision table and a lost-reply exercise.

title: Do not turn conversational tasks into a durability guarantee
observed: Tools and workflow lessons use several unverified construction or transition forms, including Agent.hand_off(), Tool.create(), Agent(tasks=...) and TaskGroup.regress(index). The installed framework does not expose those forms as presented. Generic type annotations are also treated too strongly as runtime validation.
correction: Teach source-correct AgentTask and task-group behavior, handoffs and tool definitions. Distinguish conversational completion, runtime data validation and persisted business execution. Guaranteed process-crash cleanup or durable recovery cannot be inferred from an in-process lifecycle hook.
book_action: Add an abstraction comparison; retain P1 as the accepted-work and effect authority.

title: A timeout does not prove external work stopped
observed: Some integration and operational teaching treats a timeout or cancelled waiter as a hard stop or a sufficient basis for fallback. That conclusion exceeds what local task cancellation establishes for threads, remote services or already-admitted calls.
correction: State who owns the underlying work, how cancellation propagates, what can still complete, and how unknown results are reconciled. Python wait_for waits for cancellation and may exceed its nominal timeout; an external side effect still needs its own identity and evidence.
book_action: Preserve the book's uncertainty rules; add graph/MCP and telephony examples without creating another recovery owner.

title: Redis coordination is not transparent media recovery
observed: Self-hosting lessons describe worker registration through Redis, all room state in Redis or stateless media nodes, unconfigured metrics on port 7880, and universal zero-downtime upgrades. These claims combine separate services and exceed the documented deployment guarantees.
correction: Separate resident media/session state, Redis coordination, the agent control connection and durable application storage. Configure a metrics endpoint explicitly. Explain draining and reconnection with their limits; node or process failure is not a promise to resume every existing conversation transparently.
book_action: Expand the existing topology and failure question. Keep the existing Redis/PSRPC/NATS distinction and do not add NATS to the POC on the basis of this course.

title: Measure turn quality and provider tradeoffs under a fixed workload
observed: Across turn detection, realtime and provider lessons, fixed latency, capacity, quality, cost or savings numbers lack a reproducible common workload. Some explanations conflate different turn detectors or describe TTS as universally deterministic.
correction: Separate VAD, endpointing, semantic turn completion and interruption recovery. Measure the selected language, noise, network, device and provider versions. Cache identity must cover all output-affecting inputs and scope; do not promise identical synthesis or a fixed saving across providers.
book_action: Add a paired provider/pipeline experiment with latency distributions, false interruption outcomes and useful-task cost.

title: A transfer, recording or webhook is evidence with limits
observed: Production-phone teaching sometimes overstates what participant events, encryption labels, in-memory call records or webhooks establish. A dial request, human answer, successful transfer and acknowledged business result are distinct observations.
correction: Define transfer commit and fallback behavior, preserve the original call/work identity, and reconcile late events. Describe SIP/media encryption per leg and endpoint. A callback history kept only in process memory until call end cannot supply crash-proof reconciliation by itself; recording authorization does not prove an artifact was retained.
book_action: Add a human-never-answers scenario and a short evidence table for phone calls and recordings.

title: Use the final assessment as practice, with explicit limits
observed: The course and final-track quiz explanations repeat some of the API and guarantee issues above. This audit did not independently establish credential recognition, hiring value, assessment identity checks or issuer endorsement.
correction: Use the questions to find weak topics, then defend an original design and failure scenario with primary sources. A quiz score cannot establish SDK execution, production correctness, voice quality or interview readiness.
book_action: Write original mock-interview questions and keep course completion out of the application prerequisites.
